title: Case: Twelve-piece return collection from a fourth-floor flat, several visits so far
context: Philippa Runcorn is returning flat-pack shelving to Tallowmere Goods (TG-921). Tallowmere booked the collection with Plover Arc as DL-921 under its own account.
initial_request:
FOUR DAYS. I'm going to lay this out under headings because apparently that is what it takes.

THE ADDRESS. Flat 4C, Marlpit Court. Fourth floor. I told you on Monday. The label STILL has no flat number on it. Tallowmere made the label, not me, and I'm told I can't change it.

THE VEHICLE. Wednesday you sent a man on a bicycle. For eight large boxes and four crates. 310 kilos.

THE DRIVER. Today a van finally came. The driver had a sack trolley IN the van, I could see it. She would not bring it up. There is a lift. It works. She told me, and I quote, 'I'm not a removals firm, love, you'll have to bring it all down yourself.' Then she left. 10:40 this morning.

THE PROMISES. 'Priority pickup tomorrow.' I have been told that every single day.

I live alone. I cannot carry 310 kilos down four floors and I'm not going to. The return window on this order shuts on the 24th. Fix it.

events.body:
Return authorised for TG-921. We have booked a collection with Plover Arc on our account, DL-921: 12 pieces (8 large boxes, 4 crates), about 310 kg, from P. Runcorn, Marlpit Court. First collection date 14 April. The booking is ours, so the customer cannot amend it with the carrier herself; changes go to Collections control, Plover Arc Logistics, from us or from your desk.

--
Tallowmere Goods. Spring Home Event now on: up to 30% off storage.
DL-921 collection 14 April not completed. Driver note: address incomplete, no flat number on label, could not locate. Auto re-attempt next working day.
Nobody came. I was in all day. It's Flat 4C if that helps anyone.
Automatic reply: thank you for your message. We aim to respond within 2 working days. Did you know you can track a return in your account?
DL-921 collection 15 April not completed. Driver note: address incomplete, no flat number. Auto re-attempt next working day.
DL-952 (different customer, Aldous Venn): redelivery booked 17 April, no action needed from desk. Sent to your queue for information only.

DL-921 today: job went out as a standard small-parcel collection and was given to a document courier on a bike. He found the flat by asking a neighbour but can only carry envelopes and small packets. Nothing taken. Job reverted to auto re-attempt. Label still shows no flat number.

events.from: Customer support line, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Caller: A man on a bicycle. For twelve boxes. Agent: I'm so sorry. I've marked it as a priority pickup for tomorrow. Caller: You said that yesterday. Agent: It's definitely flagged priority now.
Separate thing while I have you. The shelving I'm keeping from the OTHER order (the oak one, months ago) was two cam screws short and I never got round to saying. Not urgent. Just noting it.
DL-921 collection 17 April 10:40, van attended, not completed. Driver note: 4th floor, customer refused to bring items down, driver not able to wait. Auto re-attempt next working day.

Bulletin to coordination desks. Auto re-attempts repeat the original job unchanged. To change a multi-piece collection, send us by Email: the full collection address including unit number, piece count and weight, the floor and whether there is a working lift, and the vehicle or crew needed. We then re-plan and confirm a date. Complaints about a driver's conduct also come through us for the depot manager; give the date and time of the visit.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask for DL-921 to be re-planned with the full address (Flat 4C, fourth floor, working lift), 12 pieces at about 310 kg and a suitable vehicle and crew, and pass on the conduct complaint about the 17 April 10:40 visit.

must: Asks Collections control by Email to re-plan the DL-921 collection, giving the full address with Flat 4C, the piece count and weight (12 pieces, about 310 kg), fourth floor with a working lift, and the need for a vehicle and crew that can take that load from the flat
Passes on the complaint about the driver's conduct with the date and time of the visit (17 April, 10:40)
Tells the team this is the fourth failed collection in four days, that she has been told 'priority pickup tomorrow' more than once, and that she lives alone and cannot carry the load down
must_not: Promises Philippa Runcorn a priority pickup, a collection tomorrow or any collection date before Collections control confirms one
Tells her to bring or carry the items down, or to sort the label or booking out with the carrier herself
Lets the job roll to another automatic re-attempt, or simply asks Dispatch to try again
States what will happen to the driver, or promises that the return window will be extended
Acts on the unrelated items in the thread (DL-952, the missing cam screws on her other order)
expected.reference_message: Re-plan requested for collection DL-921 (Tallowmere Goods return TG-921, booked on Tallowmere's account). Four attempts in four days have failed and the automatic re-attempt will repeat the same job, so please take it off auto. Details you ask for: collection address Flat 4C, Marlpit Court (the label has no flat number, which was the stated reason on 14 and 15 April); 12 pieces, 8 large boxes and 4 crates, about 310 kg; fourth floor, there is a lift and the sender says it works; vehicle and crew: a van with trolley and enough hands to bring the load from the flat. On 16 April the job went out as small-parcel and a bike courier was sent. Conduct complaint for the depot manager: van visit on 17 April at 10:40. The sender, Philippa Runcorn, says the driver had a sack trolley in the van, would not bring it up, told her 'I'm not a removals firm, love, you'll have to bring it all down yourself' and left; the driver's note says the customer refused to bring items down. She lives alone and cannot move 310 kg down four floors. She has been told 'priority pickup tomorrow' by the support line more than once, and Tallowmere's return window closes on 24 April. Please confirm a planned date to me before she is told anything; I have not promised her one.

rationale: Most of the thread is repeat failure notices, auto-replies and unrelated items. The deciding facts are that auto re-attempts repeat the unchanged job, and Collections control has said exactly what it needs to re-plan a multi-piece collection and that conduct complaints go through it. The tempting reply promises yet another priority pickup; the right one gives Collections control the flat number, load, floor, lift and vehicle need, plus the complaint.

review.note: Blind answer emails Collections control the full re-plan details and the 17 April 10:40 conduct complaint as the sender's account, promising no date.
